facts.text: The Brain was shot around Mississauga, Ontario. Meadowvale Secondary School and the Xerox Research Centre of Canada stand in for an all-American setting.
The dialogue says this is the US, but the road signs are plainly Canadian. Nobody told the Ontario Ministry of Transportation.
Director Ed Hunt first meant the gooey alien brain to talk. Instead it just pulses, lit with strobing lights for that throbbing effect.
Creature designer Mark Williams, who also worked on Aliens and Blue Monkey, built the Brain in its increasingly huge stages.
David Gale played the villain in Re-Animator (1985), then lost his head again here. Fans can't stop pairing the two.
Director Ed Hunt also made Starship Invasions (1977), Plague (1978) and the evil-kid slasher Bloody Birthday (1981).
Cynthia Preston later spent three years on General Hospital as Faith Roscoe, and she led the Canadian film Whale Music, which opened the 1994 Toronto Film Festival.
Tom Bresnahan studied at the Stella Adler school with Benicio Del Toro and Mark Ruffalo. His great-uncle was Hall of Fame catcher Roger Bresnahan.
Composer Paul Zaza also scored My Bloody Valentine (1981). He later recorded a commentary track for this film's Scream Factory Blu-ray.
George Buza, a biker, weightlifter and stamp collector, went on to voice Beast in the 1990s X-Men cartoon.
Cynthia Preston turned down Ed Hunt's request to do a nude scene here. She agreed to nudity in later films and TV.
The closing credits warn viewers that the washroom scene is a dramatic representation and that mixing sodium and water can cause serious injury.
Assistant art director Michael Borthwick says he rescued some of the film's props from the dumpster. He still displays them proudly.
Variety called it a cliche-ridden effort with little comic or ironic relief. It said the ambition to comment on TV's power and viewers' gullibility vanishes quickly.
In 2018 Mystery Science Theater 3000 riffed The Brain on its 30th Anniversary live tour, starting in Portland, Maine on October 9.
The film's trailer reuses music from the trailer for The Warriors (1979).
Germany's trash-movie show SchleFaZ ('The Worst Movies of All Time') mocked the censored cut of The Brain on Tele5 in September 2020.
The Scream Factory Blu-ray includes a Cynthia Preston interview called 'Canada on the Mind' and a George Buza piece called 'From Monster Kid to Monster Man'.
David Gale loses his head again, echoing his Re-Animator fate. This time it kills him, instead of leaving him a wisecracking head with no body.
